name: Pier 96
summary_en: Pier 96 is a container terminal the city has spent fifty years trying to keep occupied. The Port's own newsletter records it returning officially to the Port in 1978, after the shipping line that had held the master lease since the pier was completed in 1971 went through bankruptcy owing what it calls a staggering $2.5 million in back rent; the Port then went looking for tenants for the combined Pier 94-96 terminal, and Evergreen took preferential berthing and back-up land for its containers. Commission agendas of the same era show the small change of running a working pier — $30,000 for spare parts for the Paceco cranes, $10,000 for an electrical contractor to direct and assist crane maintenance, bids for repairs to a fork-lift at the Lighter Freight Station. The solicitations never really stopped: the Port issued a request for proposals in 2007 for a maritime terminal operation on approximately fifteen acres with 800 linear feet of berth space, and another in 2014 for a bulk export maritime terminal. What is missing is money. The Port's 10-year capital plan lists $15,377,000 of work needed at Pier 96 with the funding source recorded as "None Identified", and names the pier among the facilities that may not be viable candidates for redevelopment given the cost of rehabilitating them. Almost nothing is recorded as spent here by name: a single $5,000 payment to an advisory firm in 2023.

Stephanie Shakofsky FROM: MoniqueMoyer iill Executive Director ^ / I SUBJECT: Request Authorization to Advertise and Issue a Request for Proposals for a Maritime Terminal Operation at Pier 96 DIRECTOR'S RECOMMENDATION: APPROVE THE RESOLUTION Overview Port staff requests authorization from the Port Commission to advertise and issue a competitive solicitation for a maritime leasing opportunity on approximately fifteen acres including 800 linear feet of berth space at Pier 96 to operate a maritime cargo terminal ("Site"). In addition to generating lease and wharfage and dockage revenues, the project will utilize a maritime terminal that has been vacant for several years. The Site's deep-water berth, on-dock rail and large vacant land parcel offers a prime maritime opportunity for the Port. Over the past year, Port staff has received numerous expressions of market interest in developing the Site for maritime uses. Location The Site is located in the Southern Waterfront at Pier 96 within the Port's 278 acre Piers 80-96 Maritime Industrial Complex. The Site enjoys some of the best industrial transportation access in San Francisco, with easy access to water, road and rail transport. The Site is surrounded by the Port's bulk cargo terminal at Pier 94 and the Port's freight rail

routes. Finally, the Site is in the vicinity of the major concrete producers in the City and County of San Francisco ("City"), which use construction materials imported through the Piers 90-96 Maritime Terminal.
